answer: Each identity buys one key-bound ticket: a 40-credit anchor bond plus a 20-credit fee, so the k-th fake still costs 60. A beacon draws winners; a drawn ticket activates, while an undrawn ticket stays hollow, its bond held till close. To field 1,000 drawn fakes at a one-in-four draw, an attacker needs 4,000 tickets, sinking 80,000 in fees and locking 160,000 in bonds. A rented-ticket ring fails: worker key must match ticket key, or the anchor bond burns. Anyone can recompute the draw from the beacon seed and ticket list. An honest agent buys one ticket and recovers its 40 bond at close.
